newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht firms late on dollar's weakness.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht firms late on dollar's weakness.

text.p: The baht firmed against the dollar near the Wednesday close following the U.S. unit's weakness in major currency markets, dealers said.
The baht rallied to 25.960/25.980 per dollar in late trade from 25.990/25.995 early in the morning, dealers said.
The baht weathered a brief morning selloff by foreign speculators as dollar's bullish sentiment prompted a new round of baht attacks, dealres said.
"The baht was hit by a brief selloff in the morning but the dollar's sharp fall significantly stemmed its slide," said one currency dealer at a European bank.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the midrate at 25.96 per dollar, its low since May 4, 1990, when it stood at 25.96, and against 25.91 on Tuesday.

The overnight interbank rate was steady at about 13.00 percent against 13.00-14.00 in the morning as funds injected through the central bank's bond repurchase window helped ease tight liquidity, dealers said.
"The overnight interbank rate would have been higher if the central bank did not offer funds through the repurchase market," said one dealer at local bank.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium fell to 14.00/15.00 satangs per dollar late from 15.50/16.50 in the morning.
